title: An invariance screen for a bridging assumption, scored as a classifier
question: Does instability across observed trials predict failure of a bridge used in a gap with no data, and does a screen on marginal effects fire under a valid bridge through non-collapsibility?
design: K trials with differing covariate laws and a gap environment; Cochran's Q screen with abstention on marginal, conditional and standardized log odds ratios; valid bridge, drift visible in the trials, and drift confined to the gap; 20 cells and 3 controls, 1000 replicates each.
answer: A stability screen across observed trials cannot confirm a bridge and refutes it rarely. With 4 or 10 trials, drift visible across them that biased the gap estimate by 0.28 was flagged in only 20% to 24% of analyses, and drift confined to the gap never above the null rate; passing the screen did not improve coverage of the reported analyses. Screening marginal log odds ratios raised false abstention under a valid bridge from 0.11 to 0.19 to 0.24 through non-collapsibility; screening conditional or standardized effects removed that.
findings: Primary confirmed: under a valid bridge with strong prognosis, marginal minus conditional abstention 0.077 (SE 0.016) with 4 trials and 0.113 (SE 0.017) with 10; standardized within 0.03 of conditional.
Visible drift of 0.15 per unit (gap bias about 0.28): abstention 0.20 to 0.24; of 0.3 per unit (gap bias about 0.56): 0.50 to 0.67.
Gap-only drift: abstention within Monte Carlo error of the valid-bridge rate while the gap estimate was biased by up to 0.60.
Coverage among analyses that passed the screen differed from coverage among all analyses by at most 0.011.
Controls: identical trials 0.099 to 0.104; collapsible risk-difference model, marginal screen 0.117; large drift 0.990 or more.
not_answered: One event-rate level, no measurement shift, Cochran's Q only; environments valid by construction. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Conditional log odds ratio in the gap environment
methods_compared: Cochran's Q screen on marginal log odds ratios
on standardized marginal log odds ratios
